questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A student hears the teacher call her name, stands up, writes the answer on the board and claps when the lesson ends. State what kind of action she is performing, and name the major region of the brain in which the decision to act is taken.

markingPoints.description: She is performing voluntary actions, which are based on deciding what to do next
The decision is taken in the fore-brain, the main thinking part of the brain

evidence:
Writing, talking, moving a chair,
clapping at the end of a programme are examples of voluntary actions
which are based on deciding what to do next.
The fore-brain is the main thinking part of the brain.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: Information from all over the body has to reach the brain and spinal cord, and instructions have to travel back to the muscles. Name the part of the nervous system that carries out this two-way communication, and name the two kinds of nerves it is made of.

markingPoints.description: The two-way communication between the central nervous system and the other parts of the body is carried out by the peripheral nervous system
It consists of cranial nerves arising from the brain and spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The peripheral nervous system; cranial nerves arising from the brain and spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.

evidence:
the central nervous system and the other parts of the body is facilitated
by the peripheral nervous system consisting of cranial nerves arising
from the brain and spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.
brain and spinal cord constitute the central nervous system (Fig. 6.3).

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: After finishing her lunch, a student says that she is no longer hungry although the food is still on the table. State the sensation that tells her she has eaten enough, and name the part of the brain in which the centre responsible for it lies.

markingPoints.description: The sensation is the feeling of being full, which comes from a centre associated with hunger
That centre lies in a separate part of the fore-brain

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The sensation of feeling full; a separate part of the fore-brain.

evidence:
The sensation of feeling full is because of a centre
associated with hunger, which is in a separate part of the fore-brain.
